stories.title: Burnham blames Brexit and Thatcher in landmark first Commons address as PM
stories.summary: Andy Burnham made his first statement to the House of Commons as Prime Minister, pledging devolution deals and 'stronger public control' of essential services, and blaming Brexit for a 'decade of low growth'. He promised to be 'relentless' in bringing public ownership of water and hinted at approving North Sea oil and gas projects.

stories.title: UK long-term borrowing costs hit 28-year high ahead of October Budget
stories.summary: Long-term government gilt yields have risen to their highest level since 1998, putting immediate pressure on Burnham's first Budget next month and limiting fiscal headroom for his spending plans.

stories.title: Burnham's ambitious plans 'need room to breathe' – but Westminster suffocates change
stories.summary: A Guardian analysis warns that Burnham's devolution agenda and No. 10 North vision face structural resistance from Whitehall, even as the PM tries to rebalance England's centre of gravity away from London.

topics.name: Burnham Gov Intelligence
topics.description: Procurement, tech/AI, spending, vendor & priority signals

stories.title: 🤖 UK government launches £100m Sovereign AI R&D procurement scheme for startups
stories.summary: The Burnham government has opened the first procurement competitions under its Sovereign AI R&D Scheme, backed by up to £100m, covering four challenge areas: compute efficiency, AI in defence, safe AI agent adoption, and NHS productivity. Contracts range from £250k–£10m, with a supplier briefing on 7 September and proposals due 1 October.

stories.title: 🤖 GDS brings in cyber firm to undertake GovAssure audit of One Login
stories.summary: The Government Digital Service has commissioned an external cybersecurity firm to audit its One Login platform under the GovAssure framework, following a period in which the platform's security setup faced setbacks and scrutiny.

stories.title: 🤖 UK government plans AI chip purchases to keep British tech firms from relocating to US
stories.summary: The government is planning to purchase AI chips and semiconductor equipment from British tech firms to help prevent AI startups from moving to the United States, as part of its broader Sovereign AI agenda.

stories.title: 🏗️ Capgemini wins £200m HMRC data warehouse contract — and questions arise over supplier concentration
stories.summary: Capgemini has won the largest contract in HMRC's £420m Data Warehouse and Integration Transformation (DWIT) programme, worth up to £200m over five years for legacy data warehouse migration. TechMarketView notes this raises questions about HMRC's dependence on a single supplier.

stories.title: 🚦 Burnham and Healey punt welfare reforms into long grass — no major benefits announcements expected before October Budget
stories.summary: Order Order reports that despite Labour's election pledges on welfare, Burnham's government is not expected to make any major announcements on the welfare and benefits bill in October's Budget, effectively pausing this reform agenda.

stories.title: 🤖 Defra trialling Microsoft Copilot to support neurodivergent staff
stories.summary: The Department for Environment, Food & Rural Affairs is piloting Microsoft Copilot as a personal AI assistant to support colleagues with neurodivergent needs, one of the first departments to do so.

topics.name: Parliament
topics.description: House of Commons & Lords debates, legislation, PMQs

stories.title: Burnham makes first Commons address: IPP prisoners, devolution, public services reform
stories.summary: PM Burnham addressed the Commons on his first full week as PM, tackling the long-running IPP (Imprisonment for Public Protection) prisoners issue, pledging devolution deals, and indicating early priorities. Tomorrow (2 Sep) will be his first PMQs.

stories.title: Public Office (Accountability) Bill — Second Reading in Lords
stories.summary: The House of Lords is considering the second reading of the Public Office (Accountability) Bill, a significant piece of legislation that would tighten standards and accountability requirements for public officials.

stories.title: Representation of the People Bill remaining stages in Commons tomorrow
stories.summary: The Commons is scheduled to consider the remaining stages of the Representation of the People Bill on 2 September, alongside Burnham's first Prime Minister's Questions.

stories.title: Keir Starmer to stand down as MP to focus on international affairs
stories.summary: Former Prime Minister Keir Starmer has announced he is resigning his Holborn and St Pancras parliamentary seat, triggering a by-election. Starmer said he wishes to focus on international defence and security work, and combating violence against women and girls.

stories.title: Burnham blames Brexit and Thatcher for UK's 'wrong turns' in first Commons speech
stories.summary: In a wide-ranging first Commons address, PM Burnham positioned his government as the corrective to decades of 'wrong turns', blaming Brexit and Thatcherite economics for the UK's low growth trajectory and inequality.

stories.title: UK social mobility watchdog could be axed as ministers plan shake-up
stories.summary: Ministers are reportedly planning a shake-up of social mobility bodies, with the UK's main watchdog potentially facing abolition as the Burnham government reviews arms-length bodies for efficiency.

stories.title: Badenoch sacks shadow chancellor Mel Stride, names Alex Burghart as deputy Tory leader
stories.summary: Conservative leader Kemi Badenoch has reshaped her shadow cabinet, removing shadow chancellor Mel Stride for 'insufficient pugnacity' on Treasury issues, and naming Alex Burghart as deputy Tory leader ahead of Burnham's first parliamentary session.

stories.title: Badenoch says Burnham's theory of growth is 'completely wrong'
stories.summary: Responding to Burnham's first Commons statement, Kemi Badenoch accused the PM of offering 'more government control, more taxes and more politicians', and argued Conservative economic theory — not more public intervention — is the answer to the UK's growth deficit.

stories.title: Badenoch visited Rome and 'fantasised' Meloni told her not to do a deal with Reform
stories.summary: Reports emerged that Badenoch's Rome visit to meet Italian PM Giorgia Meloni did not result in any formal signal against a Reform-Conservative pact — despite Badenoch suggesting as much publicly, leaving her looking 'shell-shocked'.

stories.title: Ed Davey calls for national commission on political reform in response to Burnham's Commons address
stories.summary: Liberal Democrat leader Sir Ed Davey used his question to PM Burnham to push for a national commission on political reform, arguing that too much power in the UK remains 'in the wrong hands'. Burnham said he does want political reform but gave no firm commitment on a commission.

stories.title: Farage faces questions over claim of second parliamentary standards investigation
stories.summary: Nigel Farage, who resigned as an MP in July citing a second standards investigation into his finances, is now facing scrutiny over that claim — the watchdog is not believed to have widened the investigation as he alleged. Farage triggered a Clacton by-election when he quit.

stories.title: Farage back as MP — reportedly to spend 'even less time in parliament'
stories.summary: After being re-elected in the Clacton by-election, Farage has reportedly told GB News employers he will spend even less time in parliament than before, raising fresh questions about his commitment to his parliamentary duties.

stories.title: Richard Tice defends Reform UK-led councils over council tax rises and cuts
stories.summary: Reform UK deputy leader Richard Tice defended the party's record in councils it now controls, after council tax rises and service cuts emerged in Reform-led authorities — contradicting Farage's earlier pledge that Reform councils would keep rises lower than rivals.

stories.title: SNP to hold private closed-door debate on party governance in wake of Operation Branchform
stories.summary: The SNP is expected to hold a behind-closed-doors session to discuss how the party is run and make improvements in the wake of Operation Branchform — the police investigation into the party's finances that led to the arrest of former chief executive Peter Murrell.

stories.title: Swinney sticks with pledge to cap prices on basic foods in Scotland
stories.summary: First Minister John Swinney has reaffirmed the Scottish Government's commitment to capping prices on basic food items, maintaining a flagship SNP policy despite cost pressures.

topics.name: Cabinet Office
topics.description: Government reshuffles, senior appointments, cross-department policy

stories.title: Tech leader Megan Lee-Devlin appointed new CEO of HM Courts and Tribunals Service
stories.summary: Megan Lee-Devlin, a technology and digital transformation leader, has been appointed as the new chief executive of HM Courts and Tribunals Service — signalling a continued focus on digital modernisation in the justice system.

stories.title: Ross Maude confirmed as Chief Digital and Information Officer, Cabinet Office
stories.summary: TechMarketView's coverage of their upcoming events reveals Ross Maude as CDIO of the Cabinet Office, a key appointment as Burnham's government focuses on digital transformation of central government.

stories.title: Starmer's resignation as MP will trigger by-election in Holborn and St Pancras
stories.summary: Keir Starmer's decision to stand down as MP for Holborn and St Pancras will trigger a by-election in a seat he held with an 11,572 majority in 2024, though that majority is expected to be tighter — with the Greens and left-wing independents mounting strong challenges.

stories.title: House of Lords Questions — Ministers face scrutiny on government priorities
stories.summary: Lords held Questions on 1 September, with government ministers facing questions on their priorities. The session followed Burnham's first Commons statement and provides a further parliamentary check on the new PM's agenda.

stories.title: Public Office (Accountability) Bill — Lords consider Part 2
stories.summary: The House of Lords continued scrutiny of the Public Office (Accountability) Bill, considering Part 2 of the legislation which addresses accountability standards for those in public life.
